outcome: The literal Williamson conjecture (that Williamson matrices — quadruples of symmetric circulant ±1 matrices A,B,C,D of order n with AA^T+BB^T+CC^T+DD^T=4nI — exist for every positive integer n) was disproven before the frozen revision, by Đoković in 1993 (order 35 counterexample) with further counterexamples (orders 47, 53, 59) found in 2008. No result since 26 January 2024 reopens, extends, or otherwise changes this settled status; nothing found in the window is a case of this specific bullet.

counterexample.object: Order 35 (and later orders 47, 53, 59): no Williamson matrices exist at these orders, contradicting the conjecture that they exist for every n.
counterexample.verified_how: Exhaustive computer search (Đoković, 1993; MathCheck SAT-solver verification of the nonexistence, independently reproducible per the MathCheck page).

summary: The Williamson conjecture as stated in the frozen Wikipedia revision (Williamson matrices exist for every positive integer n) was already refuted in 1993 by Đoković, who found via exhaustive computer search that no Williamson matrices exist at order 35 — the smallest known counterexample at the time — with further counterexamples at orders 47, 53 and 59 found by 2008. Both of these events predate the 26 January 2024 snapshot, so status is open_stale and no post-window change to the conjecture itself was found. I checked two lines of post-2024 work the triage flagged as possibly relevant, and both turn out to be results about neighboring problems rather than this bullet, per the §3.1 scope rule (a related/variant problem does not count): (1) Kharaghani, Mohammadian and Tayfeh-Rezaie, 'A search for Hadamard matrices of Williamson type' (arXiv:2605.08661, submitted 9 May 2026), which studies 'near Williamson matrices' — a deliberately relaxed definition (only A is required circulant; B, C, D are symmetric circulant but the joint structure differs from classical Williamson matrices) — and classifies all inequivalent near-Williamson quadruples for odd orders up to 35 and proves existence up to 63, plus a new quaternary Hadamard matrix of order 118 as a corollary. This is a variant construction with a changed definition, not a case of the stated conjecture (which is already settled/refuted), and I found no AI/ML involvement in this paper — its abstract, methodology, and metadata show only computer search (no mention of AI or ML models). (2) The August 2026 announcement by Levent Alpöge (Anthropic), Philippe Voinov and Saul Reynolds-Haertle, using Claude, of Hadamard matrices for the 12 previously-open orders below 2000 (668, 716, 892, 1132, 1244, 1388, 1436, 1676, 1772, 1916, 1948, 1964), posted as an encoded puzzle on X on 12 August 2026 and tracked (provisionally, as 'solved by AI') by Epoch AI's FrontierMath open-problems tracker. This is a result about the parent Hadamard conjecture, not the Williamson conjecture: the search frontier for order 668 specifically is described (via Đoković and Kotsireas' reduction, and corroborated by an independent paper 'Order 668 in the Hadamard conjecture: structural bottlenecks and a certified local-search obstruction') as Goethals-Seidel difference families over Z/167Z in the quadratic-residue-anchored skew supplementary-difference-set regime — a fundamentally different construction from Williamson matrices, which the same source-family explicitly notes are 'too sparse to generate Hadamard matrices of all feasible orders.' No source ties the order-668 (or the other 11) construction to Williamson-type matrices. This belongs to the hadamard-conjecture record, not this one. I could not fully verify the order-668 claim's own status: TheoremDB (accessed via WebFetch) states 'No real Hadamard matrix of order 668 is known, and no nonexistence proof is known,' crediting only Eliahou's 2025 64-modular (not exact) construction, while Epoch AI describes the August 2026 Claude-assisted construction as an actual solution, marked 'provisionally' as AI-solved pending confirmation of how much mathematical insight came from Claude versus the three-person human team. This dispute (and the AI-role classification) is properly a finding for the hadamard-conjecture record, since it is about the parent conjecture, not this one — I note it here only because the triage record raised it under this key.
competing_reading: One could argue the near-Williamson-matrices paper (2605.08661) is close enough in name and spirit to count as progress on 'the problem of finding Williamson matrices' as loosely worded in the Wikipedia statement. I read the statement as referring to the specific mathematical object (Williamson matrices proper, as defined by Williamson in 1944 and by the Wikipedia article's own definition), for which the near-Williamson class is an explicitly different, relaxed structure introduced by the authors themselves as a new object — a related problem, not a case, under §3.1. If a future reader considers 'near Williamson matrices' close enough to count, this would shift to progress/partial with ai_role none (since no AI was used in that paper regardless).
what_would_settle_it: A source explicitly stating that the near-Williamson-matrices existence results are understood by the field as bearing on the classical Williamson conjecture (rather than as a distinct relaxed construction), or a source tying the order-668/Claude construction specifically to a Williamson-type (symmetric circulant quadruple) matrix rather than a Goethals-Seidel/difference-set construction.
